sort:mondo/disease.collapses: Everything the ontology says about a concept (definition, synonyms, subclass edges, cross-references, deprecation) is collapsed to one identifier at release 2026-05-05.
sort:mondo/disease.licenses: Naming a disease concept of the Mondo Disease Ontology as a claim party or as a scope value. The kernel always checks identifier syntax (mondo: and seven digits, lower case) where a referent is typed, and checks membership only against a member list the caller supplies.
sort:mondo/disease.not_established: That a term is a member when no list was supplied, that a supplied list is the complete release, or that a member is fit for new use (the release holds deprecated terms). A disease concept is not a case definition, a patient or a cohort. No kernel comparison reads subclass edges or synonyms, so a broader neighbouring term such as mondo:0100320 is a different term and no substitute. The upstream spelling MONDO: is outside the identifier class; converting it is a recorded step of any member derivation, and a member list left in the upstream spelling makes every canonical term a non-member without any refusal.
